title: Magnets in zero gravity
question: What shapes do randomly scattered magnets make when nothing but their own pull acts on them?
line: Thirty 5 mm ferrite ball magnets start at random places, pointing random ways, in a 15 cm box with no gravity. Each ball is a perfect magnetic dipole: it pulls, pushes and twists every other one with the real dipole law, which falls off as 1/r⁴. Teal is the north half and amber the south. Watch them swing round, snap together nose to tail and grow into chains, rings and clumps. It plays in slow motion (¼ speed), because real magnets snap together in a blink. Turn up the strength toward neodymium and they snap even harder.
